_comment: Canonical substrate-of-substrate dependency DAG (ADR-0280 §D-1, the v1.0.0 Tier-1 worked example populated VERBATIM). Single source of truth for substrate dependency direction, bootstrap ordering (Kahn topo-sort), failure-cascade rules (ADR-0176 brown-out), SLO composition, and build-time client-crate validation; every derived surface (per-microservice manifests, bootstrap scripts, SLO compositions, Cedar permit catalogs) derives from this file. Acyclicity is the invariant (Tarjan SCC; the validator also proves bootstrap_order is a VALID topological order via Kahn — every dependency precedes its dependent). DATA, not code: canonical-json governed, reachability-registered, council-architecture owned. BOOTSTRAP-ORDER FINDING (verified): the §D-1 bootstrap_order is a hand-authored VALID topological order but it is NOT the pure alphabetical-tie-break Kahn sort that ADR-0280 §D-4 prose calls 'unique' — cloud-secrets depends only on cell at runtime (so alphabetically it would sort 2nd, before identity), yet §D-1 places it at step 5 because it is provisioned AFTER identity via the Shamir-genesis bootstrap-only seam (R-5). The alphabetical Kahn sort derived from this DAG is cell->cloud-secrets->identity->tenancy->policy-engine->audit-chain->observability->ontology->intelligence->workflow-engine, which diverges from the declared order at the cloud-secrets/identity positions. This is an internal tension in ADR-0280 between §D-1's verbatim order and §D-4's alphabetical-tie-break claim; the acyclicity lane therefore validates VALID-TOPO-ORDER (the load-bearing invariant, accommodating the R-5 seam), not equality to the alphabetical sort, and surfaces the alphabetical sort as a derived suggestion. Reported, not forced. NODE NAMING (ADR-0562 amendment): nodes use de-branded capability slugs; the §D-1 ten Tier-1 node names ARE the de-branded names and align with specs/capability-registry.json dag_node/dag_nodes: cell->cell, identity->iam(identity), tenancy->tenancy, policy-engine->policy(policy-engine) (ADR-0615 policy-extraction amendment: policy-engine is owned by the standalone policy capability, not iam), cloud-secrets->secrets(cloud-secrets), audit-chain->audit, observability->observability, ontology->data(ontology), intelligence->intelligence, workflow-engine->workflow(workflow-engine). RECONCILIATION of the capability-registry flagged_boundaries note (intelligence/workflow/iac/tenancy 'proposed' dag-nodes): tenancy, intelligence, and workflow-engine are ALREADY present in ADR-0280 §D-1's Tier-1 ten and are hereby RESOLVED (the registry flag predated reading §D-1, which already carries them). The fourth, iac (registry dag_node 'iac'; ADR-0280 Appendix C names it 'cloud-iac', tier_subtype substrate-iac), is a TIER-2 substrate (consumed at deploy time, not on the bootstrap critical path) and is therefore FORWARD-DECLARED per ADR-0280 Appendix C — it lands in DAG v1.1.0, NOT this v1.0.0 Tier-1 file, exactly as the ADR mandates (adding it here would diverge from the verbatim §D-1 ten-node Tier-1 example). All Tier-2 (cloud-iac, cloud-k8s, network, api-gateway, comms-email, consent-graph, compliance, governance, marketplace-catalog) and Tier-S5 substrate-meta (the self-hosting meta-substrate; de-branded node delivery-fabric per the ci capability) nodes are forward-declared per Appendix C and absent from v1.0.0 by design. TELEMETRY/AUDIT RECURSION-BREAK: observability sits in the bootstrap order below ontology/intelligence/workflow-engine, but its cascade weight on those higher substrates is BROWNOUT (edges *->observability carry cascade_rule=BROWNOUT, dependency_weight<=0.3, ADR-0176 brown-out) — telemetry loss is recoverable, never hot-path. observability and audit-chain are kept OFF policy-engine's hot-path (see forbidden_edges_assertion policy-engine->observability and policy-engine->audit-chain). The named bring-up breaks are encoded as forbidden_edges_assertion {from,to,reason} entries whose reason text records the bootstrap-only-seam rationale: cloud-secrets->identity (KMS owns its own Raft / Shamir-shared genesis is a bootstrap-only seam, NOT a runtime edge) and the cell-leaf assertions (single-Raft bootstrap-metastore floor: cell is the leaf, nothing higher may be its dependency). No new schema field is introduced (the §D-1 schema's forbidden_edges_assertion items are EXACTLY {from,to,reason}; the prose 'bootstrap_seam' field mentioned in ADR-0280 R-2 is NOT a schema property and is deliberately NOT emitted). TOPOLOGY FORK (ADR-0562 §8 Fork 1) RESOLVED 2026-07-10 (ADR-0280 §D-13 substrate plane-topology amendment): ADR-0280 §D-1 (this file) is the sole canonical substrate topology authority — the C-plane steady-state runtime dependency graph, with the 'cell' node understood as the cell.envelope (B0) runtime face per the §D-13 plane model. specs/platform-architecture.json substrate_dag_canonical_ordering previously encoded an INCOMPATIBLE inverted orientation (cell at stratum S2 with audit-chain/observability/cloud-secrets as S0 leaves); it has been rewritten as an explicit derived mirror (projection_kind=derived-mirror, canonical_source=/specs/substrate-dependency-dag.json) that carries this file's bootstrap_order verbatim, a DAG-consistent dependency-depth stratification (cell at S0 leaf; no node below a node it depends on), and the Tier-2 + Tier-S5 meta nodes placed by §D-13 plane and marked forward-declared (they gain computed strata positions when their edges land in DAG v1.1.0). The two SSOTs now agree by construction. This file's nodes/edges/bootstrap_order are UNCHANGED by the resolution (acyclicity + valid-topological-order invariants preserved). The plane/face-split model (E0/B0/C0/C1/C2 + G + R, the five edge-typed graphs, and the per-capability face-splits) is authored in ADR-0280 §D-13 and FLAGGED there for a DAG-schema extension (per-node plane/face fields, a genesis/provisioning/publication/failure graph set) in DAG v2 rather than forced into this v1.0.0 artifact; policy already owns its own node here (policy-engine, distinct from identity), consistent with the founder policy-extract ruling (24 capabilities <-> 24 dag_nodes). Authority: ADR-0280 (doctrine) as amended by ADR-0520 + ADR-0562; ADR-0176 (brown-out); specs/capability-registry.json (de-branded names).

edges.rationale: Identity issuance requires cell-local Postgres + KMS slot resolution.
Tenancy resolves home_cell on every tenant lookup.
Tenant admission verifies admin principals against identity.
Cell-local Postgres + Valkey shared by fragment registry.
Fragment publishers' principals resolved via identity.
Tenant context required for tenant-overlay evaluation.
KMS slot lives in cell-local HSM partition.
Audit Merkle log persisted to cell-local object store.
Audit entries seal the emitting principal's identity.
Tenant scope tagged on each Merkle leaf; falls back to 'unscoped' on tenancy brown-out.
Audit-chain admission gated by Cedar (per ADR-0243 §D-1).
Audit Merkle root sealed with Ed25519 key from KMS.
Per-cell Mimir/Loki/Tempo storage.
Per-principal metric attribution; degrades to 'unknown' on identity brown-out.
Per-tenant rollups; degrades to 'unscoped' on tenancy brown-out.
Query authorization through Cedar.
TLS certs + storage encryption keys.
Observability emits its own audit on configuration changes; tolerates degraded audit.
Per-cell Postgres + Valkey for projections.
Caller identity required for projection authorization.
Tenant scope determines projection shard.
Every projection read/write gated by Cedar.
Per-tenant field-level encryption keys.
Every state-changing projection emits an audit seal.
Metric emission tolerates dropped samples.
GPU/CPU compute allocated per-cell.
Caller identity required for inference authorization + cost attribution.
Tenant scope determines model selection + quota.
Data-class → provider routing (per ADR-0243 §D-1.1).
provider-BYOK API keys + encryption-BYOK envelope keys.
Every inference emits an audit seal with provider + cost attribution.
RAG retrieval reads from Ontology projections.
Per-inference latency metrics tolerate drops.
Per-cell durable execution state.
Workflow initiator identity required for step authorization.
Per-tenant workflow isolation.
Every step gated by Cedar.
Step encryption keys + outbound webhook secrets.
Every step transition emits an audit seal.
Workflows read/write Object Type instances.
Per-step metrics tolerate drops.
AI-step nodes call intelligence; non-AI workflows tolerate intelligence outage.

identity precedes tenancy in bootstrap; reverse edge would cycle.
identity must bootstrap before Cedar can gate calls.
audit-chain depends on policy-engine, not the reverse; cycle forbidden.
observability emits to its own audit-chain; policy-engine MUST NOT depend on observability for hot-path evaluation.
policy-engine MUST NOT depend on ontology — Ontology depends on policy-engine for authorization (the historical inversion this ADR explicitly closes).
cloud-secrets is bootstrap-step-3; identity is bootstrap-step-2. Cloud-secrets has a bootstrap-only seam to identity (Shamir-shared genesis) but no runtime dependency.
audit-chain MUST NOT depend on ontology; Merkle log is self-contained.
audit-chain MUST NOT depend on intelligence — the audit substrate is the simplest possible.
audit-chain MUST NOT depend on workflow-engine; audit emission is synchronous per-call.
RAG reads flow Intelligence → Ontology, not the reverse.
Workflows read/write Ontology; Ontology MUST NOT depend on workflows.
Workflows compose intelligence steps; intelligence MUST NOT depend on workflows.
